description: The Codified Directive establishes harmonised company formation requirements for PLCs.
The Codified Directive codifies the Second Directive's capital maintenance rules.
Distribution restrictions are set out in the Codified Directive.
Share buyback rules and treasury share restrictions originate in the Codified Directive.
The prohibition of financial assistance for PLCs is codified in 2017/1132.
The Codified Directive mandates a general meeting when net assets fall below 50% of subscribed capital.
Cross-border merger procedures are established in the Codified Directive (originally Tenth Directive).
The Codified Directive mandates the Business Registers Interconnection System.
Qualified majority thresholds for fundamental decisions are set in the Codified Directive.
Directive 2019/2121 amends the Codified Directive to add cross-border conversion and division procedures.
The Cross-Border Mobility Directive introduces the harmonised cross-border conversion procedure.
The Cross-Border Mobility Directive introduces harmonised cross-border division procedures.
Directive 2019/2121 updates the existing cross-border merger rules in the Codified Directive.
Anti-abuse safeguards for cross-border operations are introduced by this Directive.
The Cross-Border Mobility Directive mandates employee participation protections.
SRD II amends and substantially expands the original Shareholder Rights Directive.
SRD II mandates say-on-pay votes for listed companies.
SRD II establishes the related-party transaction approval and disclosure regime.
SRD II grants issuers the right to identify shareholders through the intermediary chain.
SRD II imposes transparency obligations on proxy advisors.
SRD II requires institutional investors to develop and disclose engagement policies.
SRD II mandates a binding shareholder vote on the remuneration policy.
SRD II requires an annual remuneration report subject to advisory vote.
SRD II enhances rules on general meetings originally set in SRD I.
SRD I establishes the foundational rules for shareholder general meetings.
SRD I sets minimum standards for exercising voting rights including proxy voting.
The Takeover Directive establishes the mandatory bid obligation.
The Takeover Directive defines squeeze-out rights in takeover contexts.
The Takeover Directive defines sell-out rights for minority shareholders.
The Takeover Directive establishes the optional board neutrality rule.
The Takeover Directive provides the optional breakthrough rule.
The Takeover Directive requires Member States to set a mandatory bid trigger threshold.
The Takeover Directive sets the permissible range for squeeze-out thresholds.
The Takeover Directive is a key instrument for protecting minority shareholders.
The Digitalisation Directive amends the Codified Directive with digital tools provisions.
The Digitalisation Directive mandates online company formation capabilities.
The Digitalisation Directive enhances BRIS with additional cross-border data exchange.
The SE Statute requires negotiation of employee involvement arrangements.
The SE Statute allows choice between one-tier and two-tier board structure.
The SE Statute references national company law provisions via the Codified Directive.
The Accounting Directive mandates consolidated financial statements for groups.
The Accounting Directive requires corporate governance statement referencing a national code.
The Accounting Directive provides the accounting framework for corporate group structures.
The Gender Balance Directive sets mandatory targets for board gender diversity.
The duty of care is a component of the overarching fiduciary duty.
The duty of loyalty is a component of the overarching fiduciary duty.
The duty of loyalty governs how directors must handle conflicts of interest.
The business judgment rule defines the safe harbour for the duty of care standard.
Compliance with the business judgment rule shields directors from liability.
Director liability arises from breach of fiduciary duties.
Breach of duty of care is a ground for director personal liability.
Breach of duty of loyalty is a ground for director personal liability.
The related-party transaction regime addresses a key category of conflicts of interest.
The say-on-pay mechanism applies to the remuneration policy via a binding vote.
The say-on-pay mechanism applies to the remuneration report via an advisory vote.
Squeeze-out rights include fair price safeguards protecting minority interests.
Sell-out rights are a protective mechanism for minority shareholders.
Qualified majority requirements protect minorities from simple majority override on fundamental decisions.
Capital maintenance doctrine restricts distributions to shareholders.
Capital maintenance rules impose conditions on share buybacks.
The financial assistance prohibition is a capital maintenance measure.
The serious loss of capital notification is a capital maintenance safeguard.
Cross-border mergers must protect existing employee participation rights.
Cross-border conversions must protect existing employee participation rights.
Cross-border divisions must protect existing employee participation rights.
Cross-border conversions are subject to anti-abuse review by the departure state.
Cross-border divisions are subject to anti-abuse review by the departure state.
Cross-border mergers are subject to anti-abuse safeguards under the amended rules.
Corporate groups are required to prepare consolidated financial statements.
Group structures create related-party transaction obligations for listed parent companies.
Voting rights are exercised at general meetings.
Corporate governance codes specify best practices for board composition.
Governance codes provide guidance on managing conflicts of interest.
The mandatory bid obligation is triggered when the threshold is crossed.
The squeeze-out right is triggered at the threshold set by the Member State.
The Commission monitors transposition and enforcement of the Codified Directive.
The Commission manages the BRIS interconnection system.
The expert group advises the Commission on company law policy matters.
The Single-Member Directive extends formation rules to single-member companies.
